audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's own defect list says it: Master Yi wins 55.24% over 143 games, yet the chart gives Maokai six of seven stages and the page is rated HARD 8/10.
audit.why: Something here is wrong — either the chart, the difficulty rating, or the sample. I cannot tell which from the kits, and flipping five or six rows on a hunch is exactly the failure mode the brief warns about. The mirror auditor on maokai__masteryi reached the same conclusion and declined to flip; changing it from my side alone would put the two directions in conflict.
audit.corrected: No chart edit. Raised in questionsForUser, matching the mirror's flag so both sides stay consistent until someone decides.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why describes Nature's Grasp as rooting 'on landing', as though it were a point ult.
audit.why: It is a colossal wall of brambles thrown from 3000 range that slowly advances forward, rooting whatever it reaches. There is no landing — it is a moving zone you walk out of sideways, which is completely different counterplay.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why rewritten with the 3000 range and the advancing wall.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two omissions and one contradiction. Maokai is UNTARGETABLE during the Twisted Advance dash — never stated. Sap Magic's heal cooldown is reduced every time he casts a spell OR is struck by an enemy spell — also never stated. And spikes[2].text says Alpha Strike dodges Twisted Advance, while report[5].t on the same page correctly says it cannot, because W is point-and-click and re-acquires you.
audit.why: The untargetable dash means your damage during his engage is wasted. The passive detail means chipping him accelerates the very sustain that beats you — it reframes 'poke him down' as a mistake. And the two layers currently give opposite answers to 'can I dodge his root'.
audit.corrected: report[5].t rewritten with the untargetable dash and the passive's cooldown refund; spikes[2].text corrected to agree with report[5].t; Twisted Advance's 14s written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: This page already rushes Executioner's Calling and explains why, which is right — Sap Magic is the reason he wins the early lane. Nothing to change.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit flags Bramble Smash as grounding and the missing-interactions file says it denies Alpha Strike. Riot's text is only 'knocks back nearby enemies with a shockwave, dealing magic damage and slowing them'.
audit.why: If Q grounds, Alpha Strike is unusable in his shockwave and the lane is even worse than written. The description does not support it, so I wrote the knockback interrupt instead of a grounding claim.
audit.corrected: Knockback stated in report[5].t; no grounding asserted. Listed in unverified.

edits.before: Highlander helps you dodge ganks, but his ult Nature's Grasp roots through it on landing and sets up a jungler to collect — his 6 is far scarier than yours.
edits.after: Highlander helps you dodge ganks, but Nature's Grasp is a wall of brambles thrown from 3000 range that roots whatever it reaches — his 6 sets up a collapse, yours does not.

edits.before: Track his W (Twisted Advance) above all — it's his only gap-close and the root that catches you out of Alpha Strike. If W is down, that's your single safe window to trade or farm aggressively; if it's up, give him nothing.
edits.after: Track Twisted Advance (W) above all — 14s at rank 1, his only gap-close and the root that catches you as Alpha Strike ends. With W down you get one safe window to trade or farm up; with it up, give him nothing.

edits.before: Alpha Strike's untargetability dodges his W root and ult only if timed on the cast — but his W is point-and-click, so once the blink ends he re-acquires and roots you. His Q knockback interrupts your approach and his passive regen out-paces Meditate. Highlander's slow-immunity does NOT stop his root.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is point-and-click and he is untargetable through the dash, so your autos whiff on his approach and the root lands as your blink ends. Bramble Smash knocks you back out of range, and Sap Magic's heal cooldown drops every time he casts or is struck by a spell — chipping him speeds up his own sustain.

edits.before: You start closing: Alpha Strike (Q) untargetability dodges Sapling Toss (E) and his Twisted Advance (W), but his tankiness and sustain still let him survive your burst — trade only when W is down.
edits.after: You start closing: Alpha Strike (Q) dodges Sapling Toss (E), but Twisted Advance (W) is point-and-click and re-acquires you as the blink ends, so trade only in the 14s while W is down.

notes: Left the level chart alone deliberately. The packet flags that Yi wins 55.24% while the chart hands Maokai six of seven stages, and the page is rated HARD 8/10 on top of that — but I cannot resolve which of the three is wrong from the kits, and the mirror auditor declined to flip it too, so flipping from my side would put the two directions in conflict. Raised as a question instead. Fixed: Nature's Grasp is an advancing wall, not a landing root; Maokai is untargetable through Twisted Advance; and the two layers disagreed about whether Alpha Strike can dodge that root.
